issue.title: sase-core still rejects '+' in clan summaries and aborts colon-arg completion on '+', assuming xprompt decoding always makes it a space
issue.description:
Two places in sase-core still assume that xprompt argument decoding always
rewrites `+` to a space. Epic sase-sn (phase sase-sn.4 in sase, sase-sn.5 in
sase-core) narrowed that substitution to the bare, unquoted `#name:a,b` colon
argument form, so the assumption is now false for `[[...]]` text blocks, quoted
values, and paren arguments.

1. `validate_literal_clan_summary` (crates/sase_core/src/axe_chop/validation.rs)
   rejects any clan summary containing `+` with
   `unrepresentable_clan_summary: clan summary must not contain '+', which
   xprompt argument decoding changes to a space`. Clan summaries are emitted by
   `AgentUnitWire::format_clan_directive` as `summary=[[{summary}]]`, a text
   block, which is exactly the form that is no longer `+`-decoded. The guard is
   obsolete and now blocks legitimate summaries such as "Split the C++ modules".

   The sibling `]]` guard on the same function is a different story: it is still
   partly needed. The terminator-position closing rule means a summary
   containing `]]` survives only when that `]]` is not followed by an argument
   terminator, so `Use ]] here, ok` still closes early. Relax the `]]` guard to
   the genuinely unrepresentable shape (a `]]` followed, ignoring whitespace, by
   `,`, `)`, `}`, or `|`) rather than removing it outright, or leave it and say
   so.

2. `colon_arg_context` (crates/sase_core/src/editor/completion.rs:3009) returns
   `None` when the typed colon-argument suffix contains `+`, so no completion is
   offered while typing a legitimate bare colon argument such as
   `#open:Application+Support`. The bare colon form is precisely the one form
   where `+` still means space, so aborting there is a UX gap, not a safety
   requirement.

Both were recorded as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on sase-sn.5 by that phase's worker.
The root cause is shared and both live in sase-core, so one worker fixes both in
one release. The fix also needs a `sase-core-rs` floor bump in the sase repo's
pyproject.toml, matching the existing ratchet convention.

task_type_fields.impact:
## Impact

A chop proposal whose clan summary contains an ordinary `+` (for example
"Split the C++ modules") is rejected at validation with a reason that is no
longer true, so the chop cannot dispatch. Users typing a bare colon argument
containing `+` get no completion. Neither is a regression -- both behaved this
way before epic sase-sn -- but both are now unnecessary restrictions on the
repaired grammar.
task_type_fields.repro:
## Repro

Clan-summary guard, in the linked sase-core checkout
(`sase repo open sase-core`) at afd1f87:

```bash
sed -n '/fn validate_literal_clan_summary/,/^}/p' crates/sase_core/src/axe_chop/validation.rs
```

shows the unconditional `if value.contains('+')` rejection. The paired test
`crates/sase_core/src/axe_chop/tests.rs:378` pins
`(json!("one+two"), "unrepresentable_clan_summary")`.

That a `+` now round-trips through the text-block form is verified from a sase
workspace with sase-core-rs 0.31.11:

```bash
./.venv/bin/python -c "
import sase_core_rs as c
p = '%clan(research.x, summary=[[Split the C++ modules]], tribe=research)\nbody'
u = c.plan_typed_launch_units(p, 'multi_prompt', 'sase')['units'][0]['payload']
print(repr(u['clan_summary']))
"
# 'Split the C++ modules'  -- the + survives; the validator would still refuse it
```

Editor completion gap:

```bash
sed -n '3000,3015p' crates/sase_core/src/editor/completion.rs
```

`colon_arg_context` bails on `value.contains('+')` before it can resolve the
active input.
